items.title: Moran's I
items.text:
Moran's I is a measure of spatial autocorrelation. It measures the degree to which a variable is correlated with itself in space. The formula for Moran's I is given by:

\[ I = \frac{N}{W} \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N} \sum_{j=1}^{N} w_{ij}(x_i - \bar{x})(x_j - \bar{x})}{\sum_{i=1}^{N} (x_i - \bar{x})^2} \]

items.title: LISA
items.text:
\[ I_i = \frac{x_i - \bar{x}}{m_2} \sum_{j=1}^{N} w_{ij} (x_j - \bar{x}) \]

Standardized Z-score:

\[ I_i = z_i \sum_{j=1}^{N} w_{ij} z_j\ \] \[ m_2 = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N} (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{N}\ \]

items.title: Kernal Density Estimation
items.text:
Formula as employed by scider:

\[\hat{\lambda}(u) = \frac{1}{\displaystyle \int_{W} k(v - u) \, dv} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{w_i}{2\pi \sigma^2} \exp\left( -\frac{\|u - x_i\|^2}{2\sigma^2} \right)\]

where:

  • \(\hat{\lambda}(u)\) is the estimated spatial intensity (cells or counts per unit area) at location \(u\).
  • \(n\) is the total number of cells (or spatial spots) in the dataset.
  • \(x_i\) represents the 2D spatial coordinates of cell \(i\).
  • \(w_i\) is the weight assigned to cell \(i\) (where \(w_i = 1\) for unweighted cell density, or equals gene expression counts when weighted by a feature).
  • \(k(\cdot)\) is the 2D smoothing kernel function (defaulting to an isotropic Gaussian kernel with bandwidth \(\sigma\)).
  • \(e(u)\) is the edge-correction factor accounting for the proportion of the kernel falling inside the tissue boundary \(W\).

items.title: Installation
items.text:
scider is hosted on Bioconductor and is available as a development version on GitHub. To install the development version, you can use the following commands in R:

pak (recommended)BiocManagerGitHub 
pak::pkg_install("bioc::scider") # (1)!
  1. If you don't have pak, check it out. I find it is the best way to manage all your packages.
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}

BiocManager::install("scider")

if (!requireNamespace("devtools", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("devtools")
}

devtools::install_github("ChenLaboratory/scider")

SpatialExperiment is the main class used as input. You cannot use original Seurat or AnnData objects. Please install this as well:

pak (recommended)BiocManager 
pak::pkg_install("bioc::SpatialExperiment") # (1)!
  1. If you don't have pak, check it out. I find it is the best way to manage all your packages.
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}

BiocManager::install("SpatialExperiment")

items.text:

We'll use the same example data used in the scider documentation2. This is a subset of Xenium Breast Cancer dataset. 

spe <- data("xenium_bc_spe") # (1)!

items.title: Starting with a SeuratObject/Visium HD
items.text:
As mentioned previously, scider expects a SpatialExperiment objects. If you have a SeuratObject, you will need to convert it first1.

## Convert to SCE
sce <- Seurat::as.SingleCellExperiment(seu)

## Extract spatial coordinates
spatialCoords <- as.matrix(
    seu@images[[img_id]]@coordinates[, c("imagecol", "imagerow")])

## Extract and process image data
img <- SpatialExperiment::SpatialImage(
    x = as.raster(seu@images[[img_id]]@image))

imgData <- DataFrame(
    sample_id = sample_id,
    image_id = img_id,
    data = I(list(img)),
    scaleFactor = seu@images[[img_id]]@scale.factors$lowres)

# Convert to SpatialExperiment
spe <- SpatialExperiment(
    assays = assays(sce),
    rowData = rowData(sce),
    colData = colData(sce),
    metadata = metadata(sce),
    reducedDims = reducedDims(sce),
    altExps = altExps(sce),
    sample_id = sample_id,
    spatialCoords = spatialCoords,
    imgData = imgData
)
# indicate all spots are on the tissue
spe$in_tissue <- 1
spe$sample_id <- sample_id
